claim:
Let \(X=\mathrm{ces}_3^{(2)}\) be \(\mathbb R^2\) with
\[
\|(x,y)\|_X=
\left(
|x|^3+\left(\frac{|x|+|y|}{2}\right)^3
\right)^{1/3}.
\]
Let \(\tau>0\) be the unique solution of
\[
3^{4/3}(1+\tau)^2
=
\tau\bigl((1+\tau)^2+8\bigr).
\]
Then the Ptolemy constant of \(X\) is
\[
C_{\mathrm{Pt}}(X)
=
\frac{\bigl(8+(1+\tau)^3\bigr)^{2/3}}
{3^{4/3}+\tau^2}
=
1.29958204360103898476109693949\ldots .
\]
An extremizing Ptolemy triple is
\[
x=(-1,0),\qquad
y=(0,-\tau),\qquad
z=(-1,-\tau).
\]
integrity: The upper bound is a global Hilbert-norm comparison whose unique interior extremum is proved analytically. The matching lower bound is an exact explicit Ptolemy triple. Numerical values are consistency checks only.
scientific_limitations: The theorem is restricted to the real two-dimensional Cesàro space at exponent 3. It does not give a general exponent formula or a higher-dimensional result. An older equivalent formulation under different normalization remains a residual bibliographic risk.
title: Exact Ptolemy constant of the cubic two-dimensional Cesàro space
